input.title: useAttachmentUpload now exposes stage, byte progress, result, cancel and reset, and useAttachmentPreview reports the download side with retry visibility

input.description: stage is idle, hashing, reserving, uploading, done or error; progress carries percent, loaded, total and indeterminate. On error progress stays put; reset aborts an in-flight transfer.

metadata.reason: Extracted from apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/09-AttachmentService.md at v6.2.2-dev.74 — React subsection: the new destructuring, stage/progress/result/error/cancel/reset, useAttachmentPreview
Presents the same stage and progress model through the React hooks, including the percent field the design-system bar expects

input.content:
```tsx
const { preprocess, upload, cancel, reset, stage, progress, result, error } = useAttachmentUpload();
```

- `stage` — `"idle" | "hashing" | "reserving" | "uploading" | "done" | "error"` (it replaced the older `status`/`UploadStatus` enum).
- `progress` — `{ percent, loaded, total, indeterminate }`. `percent` is 0–100, matching the design-system progress bar; `loaded`/`total` are raw bytes for a "3.2 / 10 MB" label; `indeterminate` is true while a stage runs whose bytes cannot be observed, and `percent` stays 0 for the whole of it.
- `result` — the `AttachmentUploadResult` once done.
- `error` — the failure, if any. **Progress is left where it stopped** rather than reset to zero.
- `cancel()` — aborts the transfer in flight; the `upload` promise rejects with an `AbortError`.
- `reset()` — returns the hook to idle, discarding result and error. A transfer still in flight is aborted, so it cannot keep streaming behind an idle UI.

`upload(results)` now calls `client.upload({ preprocessed: results })`, so progress, dedup reporting and cancellation are identical to the non-React path. The two-call split (`preprocess` then `upload`) is deliberate: **the ref must reach the document before the bytes are committed**, and since the ref only exists after `preprocess` resolves, submission is async — a ref cannot be produced inside a synchronous action input. `useAttachments()` returns one client per service, shared across every consumer.

`useAttachmentPreview()` reports the same shape for the download side plus retry visibility: `stage`, `progress`, `attempt`, `maxAttempts`, and `lastError` — the failure of an attempt that is about to be retried, exposed while the hook is still loading. It aborts the download on unmount.
